canonical_name: Finite complex Schur triangularization theorem family
literal_source_claim_en: A complex square matrix can be unitarily triangularized.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix the finite dimension or ordered index type, upper-versus-lower triangular convention, unitary predicate, star and matrix-multiplication conventions, conjugation orientation, equality direction, existential witness shape, or zero-dimensional case. Schur's primary Satz I is broader in scalar domain and lower-triangular in its display, while Axler Theorem 6.38 is a complex operator-and-orthonormal-basis form; neither source-to-catalog specialization/orientation nor matrix/unitary transport is accepted. Selecting one exact proposition at intake would add unstated mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix square complex matrices on Fin n or another finite linearly ordered index, or finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and endomorphisms, together with universes and typeclass conventions.
conclusion: Prospective family only: every source-specified finite complex square matrix admits a unitary change of basis making its matrix upper triangular. Exact witnesses, triangular predicate, conjugation equation, and boundary cases are unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
